look_here_first: Look at habit, stipules and inflorescence. Palmleaf poppymallow is an erect-to-weakly-erect perennial with persistent linear-lanceolate stipules, a racemose flower arrangement, no involucellar bractlets, and deeply palmately divided leaves with 3–5 main lobes.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: perennial with thick storage taproot and several stems from the base

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: stems erect to weakly erect, often glaucous and nearly glabrous

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaves palmately 3–5-lobed, often further divided into narrow segments

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: calyx lobes valvate in bud and form a pointed/apiculate bud

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: petals usually reddish-purple but sometimes white/pink; flower color not reliable alone

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: mericarps indehiscent, glabrous or sparsely hairy; beaks variable

lookalikes.differences: Callirhoe digitata: C. digitata usually has 5–10-lobed leaves, caducous stipules and a paniculate inflorescence; C. pedata usually has persistent stipules and a raceme. Current Kew/FNA distributions place C. digitata outside Texas. Callirhoe involucrata: C. involucrata is low/trailing and has 3 involucellar bractlets; C. pedata is erect and lacks involucellar bractlets. Callirhoe leiocarpa: C. leiocarpa is annual/biennial with dehiscent strongly beaked mericarps; C. pedata is perennial with indehiscent fruit.
